Is Wakie actually a good anonymous voice chat app to talk to strangers? My honest review after 2 years Have some thoughts built up after 2 years and over a thousand calls, so figured I'd share what's good and what sucks.
I'm an average looking guy and didn't have a real relationship until 25, had some virtual thing on Discord before but that doesn't really count. I tried tinder and hinge, got nowhere, I wasn't really into hookup culture but not gonna lie- my ego was bruised. I thought I was at least somewhat above average. Apparently not lol

I was fine with people I already knew but had trouble talking to strangers, covid made my phone anxiety worse, I'd ask people to text instead of call. When I started looking for work I realized how f*ed my social skills were.
Remembered Omegle and chatroulette, looked for alternatives without video, found some voice chats but too many horny old dudes and trolls, kept searching and found wakie where at least people had some rating system, downloaded it.

Around that time I was playing Genshin Impact and practicing voice acting, got decent at it, figured I'd test it on random calls. I was a bit nervous before my first call on the app but got used to it fast, I didnt try hard, just acted normal, people gave me positive ratings. Started trying voice stuff with girls and suprisingly it worked, lot of them added me to favorites, even dated one - didn't last but it was my first real relationship. Idk if it works for everyone but it worked for me, my social skills got better, I got a decent job where I don't stress too much but show up on calls. If you want instant convos and don't mind camera- ometv might work better, if looks are your thing- stick to video apps. Otherwise try wakie I guess, depends what you're working with.

Weil Cornell reproductive center **I’m very disappointed with my experience at Weill Cornell Reproductive Medicine, and I think people deserve to know what to expect.**



**My doctor, Hey Joo Kang, saw me in person during my first IVF cycle, but during my second cycle I’ve only seen her through Zoom. My case is more complex — fibroids, a tilted uterus, and ovaries that are hard to visualize — so consistent, hands-on care actually matters. Instead, every appointment feels unpredictable. I constantly have to re-explain my situation to new physicians, and many appointments felt rushed or disconnected.**



**There were a few times I went in for monitoring and was supposed to receive a call with medication instructions — instructions that are time-sensitive and crucial for success. Instead, no one contacted me, and I had to call the emergency line just to get basic guidance. That should never happen at a fertility clinic of this size.**



**Communication after my second egg retrieval was just as poor. I waited over a week with no update on my embryos. When they finally called, all they said was that five were frozen — no details. I had to email out of frustration to get the information I should have been told upfront. I constantly had to advocate for myself.**



**The billing department has been the worst part of this entire experience. No one explained that a frozen transfer is much more expensive than a fresh one. No one told me that Weill Cornell is significantly more expensive than most clinics. They also never warned me that I was nearing my yearly insurance max. Instead, they let me go through an entire stimulation cycle and egg retrieval, and now — just a week before transfer — they suddenly tell me I owe $4,993 out of pocket.**



**To make matters worse, they billed my insurance in a way that used my IVF benefit limit for services that should NOT have been billed under my IVF limit, draining my $25k IVF coverage much faster than necessary. There was no transparency or accountability.**



**And what really shocked me: they refused to move forward with my transfer until the $4,993 was paid in full.**

**Most fertility clinics offer payment plans or financial flexibility, especially during active treatment — but Weill Cornell doesn’t. They offered nothing. No plan, no options, no compassion.**



**Overall, the communication is inconsistent, the care feels impersonal, and the billing department has zero empathy or transparency. After everything, I’m transferring myself — and my frozen embryos — to another clinic that is more affordable, more supportive, and truly patient-centered.**

My experience using a red-light cap after years of bleaching  here’s what actually changed I wanted to share a genuine review because I spent months wondering if red-light therapy could help with scalp health after years of bleaching. My hair story is basically the same as a lot of people who bleach: I loved the look, but over time the top of my head started feeling weaker. My new growth felt softer and almost “thin,” not in a medical way, just noticeably different in texture and strength.

Conditioners fixed the dry ends, but nothing I tried really changed the way my *roots* felt. I didn’t want to overload my scalp with too many products, so I started looking into tools people use for basic scalp support. That’s how I ended up trying the [Welzo Red Light Cap](https://welzo.com/products/red-light-infrared-cap).

I didn’t go into it expecting miracles. I used it just because it seemed like a simple, non-chemical way to maybe encourage healthier new growth.

Here’s what actually happened over a few weeks:

**• Week 1–2:**  
Honestly, nothing dramatic. I used it while watching TV. The warmth felt relaxing, but I didn’t notice changes in my scalp or hair texture yet.

**• Week 3–4:**  
This is when I started noticing tiny differences. My roots didn’t feel as “fragile” when I touched them. When I brushed my hair, it felt like the new growth had a bit more grip instead of that overly soft, processed feel. Not thicker — just slightly stronger.

**• Week 5–6:**  
I noticed that the areas near my part line felt less delicate. My scalp also felt calmer overall. Again, nothing overnight or dramatic, but I could feel my new growth wasn’t as flimsy as before.

**• Current verdict:**  
It didn’t magically fix years of bleaching (and I didn’t expect it to), but it genuinely did something for the *texture* and *strength* of new growth. The biggest change was that the fresh hair coming in didn’t feel as fragile. It just felt “healthier,” like the scalp was happier.

Red-light therapy won’t replace good haircare routines, but as a supportive tool, I actually think it helped me in a gradual, subtle way.

**So overall:**

text:
Five Towns College (five clowns) is the worst college ever, do not EVER think of going, a waste of money, a waste of time, and something you WILL regret. I attended Five Towns for about two weeks before dropping out because of how bad it was. I felt like I got demoted from where I was when I graduated high school. I graduated with a 4.0 GPA, received a pretty scholarship (20k a year) from the desperate, money hungry people at five towns, and accidentally put myself in a horrible situation that I do not wish on any student with a passion for art, music, or anything else for that matter. 

My tuition for the semester was about 4k, and I only received back $1,900. It was supposed to be a 60 percent refund. The president of the college refuses to refund anymore of the money. I only attended classes for two weeks. It was not worth that much money, and I feel absolutely robbed. The happier part to my story is that I got out of five towns before it was too late. I took what I could get back and ran. Please do not put yourself in this situation, it is so disheartening. Even the women who worked in the advising office at told me that my best option was to drop out, that my full potential could not be met at five towns. 

I was so unsure about attending this college that I made myself sick about it so many times. The day that I went to register for classes and got my ID card, I got sick with some sort of stomach bug (I think it was a sign from somewhere warning me not to go.) If that sounds crazy to you, just continue reading!! I also had multiple nightmares where I was screaming that I did not want to go to five towns, and I would wake up feeling absolutely sick mentally and also throwing up from the stress. This was over the summer after I had already committed to the college, and all of my friends had big plans for themselves at great colleges. I just knew something was wrong. I did not want to go, I was absolutely killing myself over it. I couldn't do anything to change it because it was too late. My parents told me to just try it out for a semester and if I did not like it, I could transfer out. If you are considering this college, and this is what your parents are saying to you, tell them of my experience and I assure you, they will change their minds. 

To start off, the people are pushy, they do not stop calling you once you apply. Not even just emailing you. They call, text, and email like a desperate ex trying to get you back. It is so pathetic. They also push all of their programs on you and barely give you any time to think about what it is that YOU want. I felt as if I got roped into the business and audio concentration program just because it was the easiest thing for them to do for me. So many of the students there feel the same way, there is just this feeling of hopelessness that plagues everyone there. No one can have a conversation without hating on the college or saying that they want to leave.

To add about the business program, it is such a joke; unfortunately, it really is sad because the teachers are all very sweet and I honestly feel bad for them. The business program consists of mostly male athletes who are there on a scholarship, or kids who have no idea what they want to do with their lives. Do not fall for this program or the audio concentration that they make so enticing. You can get a much better education at one of the amazing SUNY schools nearby, even SUNY Farmingdale if business or even communications is what you want to go for. They also have visual arts programs that five towns offers, and they have even more variety. SUNY Stony Brook also offers music and SO MANY arts majors, it is outstanding and so wonderful. It is also MUCH cheaper than five towns, you will have an actual college experience, and the college that YOU are paying will actually invest in you instead of investing in themselves. Out of all of the friends I made there, they all also want to transfer out because they know they deserve better. One of my friends dropped out just as I did, and another one of my friends is also transferring out at the end of the semester. 

What was extremely alarming to me at my time there was how small the college was and how there are not even 1,000 students, maybe 500. I'm not really sure how the college is still running. The accreditation should be taken away. I attended a department mixer for business, and each year (freshman-senior) stood before the rest of the department year by year. The freshman class was the biggest one and as you got down to the seniors, two people stood. I felt so sick. I knew I had to get myself out of there. They explained that they "lost" a couple of students over the years, and of course when you put it together, these are the students that got out and realized there were better opportunities for them. Those are the lucky ones, and I am one of them. 

If you are looking for an exciting college experience with student life funded and supported, do not choose five clowns. Choose any other college, I guarantee you it will be much better. I almost wish high schools could exclude five towns from their college fairs. This should not even be an option for passionate and talented high school students getting ready to face the real world. They lie to you, they manipulate you, and they only want your money. Not to mention, five towns credits barely transfer to other colleges, so if you are thinking of just "trying it out" for a semester, don't. If you are at all unsure of what you want to do with your life or career, do not choose this school, you are putting yourself in a prison. You will waste your time, money, and your passion might even feel like it is dissipating. It definitely drained the life out of me.

It is a FOR PROFIT institution, read that loud and clear. All private colleges are, but what makes five clowns different is the fact that it quite literally is just money hungry people feeding on profit, not giving enough funding to the arts, and honestly not even understanding how to run a college whatsoever. They sell you on the audio program, which is a load of crap. The access students have to the studios is so limited and also nothing is ever taken seriously. The audio part also does not go on your degree. They do the bare minimum. Everything is the bare minimum. The food, the dorms, the curriculum, the student life. 

When I say that the food is BAD, I mean it. The cafeteria was smaller than the one at my high school, and the limited options were insane. I felt so bad for the kids who chose to dorm and that is their only option. If you choose to dorm at this college and have no car, you are quite literally putting yourself in a prison. Long Island is so wonderful and full of things to do, but this college is in the middle of a suburban neighborhood on LI. You cannot walk anywhere, it will take forever. 

I also know many people who are upperclassman at five towns who regret their choice to stay. They feel that they also could have gotten better educations and more opportunities elsewhere. They only stay now because they have dug themselves a hole. They put so much money into the school of credits that will barely transfer anywhere else, so they have no choice but to finish it.

At the end of the day, do not EVER choose this college. I don't care if you're confused, stuck on the money end of things, or looking for an easy way out. You deserve better. Money is not the most important thing in life, it comes and goes. Experience stays with you, the environment you are putting yourself in will mold you into who you are. Choose a good one. Choose a place that makes you feel like you can do anything, that you can reach for the stars, have opportunities, and dream. Do not put yourself in a situation where you think about what could have been. If you are not happy with your environment during such formative years, you will have trouble in the future. Life is short. Go somewhere that you can change your mind. One day you may be a STEM major and decide that you hate science and want to be immersed in the arts or humanities instead. Five Towns is not the college you can change your mind at or customize your education. Go somewhere that really supports your dream, and you will never regret that decision. I promise.

Much Better Adventures - Ultimate Adventure in British Columbia and Vancouver Island I participated on the September 2025 trip. This is a new MBA trip and had only run once before in June 2025. My experience of this trip and MBA was disappointing.

Not to mention, being required to dry out the tents and clean out the trailer and van at the end of the trip albeit MBA did acknowledge that this had crossed the line. 

If you decide to book this trip, be aware that unless the itinerary has been changed, you are likely to spend a lot of your time putting tents up and down, packing and unpacking the trailer, packing and unpacking day packs and own luggage for each day, eating and washing up and bear prevention rather than enjoying being in each location in the present moment. It was such a shame because Canada is stunning but the cumulative negative points of this trip overshadowed what otherwise should have been a once in a lifetime holiday. 

I gave detailed feedback to MBA and eventually settled on an agreed level of compensation payment but this did take time and the 'host' supplier/MBA tried to settle at a low level initially. 

Anyone booking through MBA needs to be aware that MBA is a booking agent only which means they are responsible for the booking but not the trip.  The 'host' supplier is responsible for delivering the trip. This is set out in the t&cs but not apparent on the face of MBA's website.

text:
Love letter to the movie Frankenstein 2025 As a huge fan of the book, when I saw the trailer, seeing Frankenstein's monster with features much closer to the book's description and clothing, I was excited that it would be a faithful adaptation. And for that very reason, I became increasingly disappointed as I watched it, a feeling that quickly changed when I realized that, unlike versions that simply take a book, strip it of its depth, and leave it empty, this is truly a coherent alternate version with a new vision of the story. It starts with the most obvious point: this work adds humanity to the "monster" and further dehumanizes the humans, not only within themselves but also in their surroundings, in how they interact with them from the very beginning. One of the reasons I loved this story is precisely because of how painful it was to see Victor so loved and the "monster" so utterly alone and despised, and here things are balanced.

Victor's past as the beloved son of a couple who adored each other and took him traveling the world, encouraging him to learn whatever he wanted, even if it was the damned science of alchemy, is erased. Now he is the son of a mother who, just like in the novel, loves him dearly, but a father who treats him with contempt and demands (it's not explicitly stated, but it's possible Victor isn't actually his son, and his parents married after he was born, judging by his treatment of him and the comment, "You bear my name and represent me," as if it were something bestowed upon him and not rather than by birth), along with a toxic relationship marked by domestic violence with his mother. From the very beginning, Victor's surroundings become less human. He grows up shouting in everyone's face that he is a genius, the complete opposite of the Victor who worked in absolute secrecy and was humiliated by his teachers for his outdated "scientific" beliefs. Instead of Clerval, his dreamy and vibrant friend. You have an arms dealer. He causes the deaths of innocents and blames the monster. He refuses to create a companion so the monster won't be alone and will have a friend by his side, feeling not a trace of empathy for him. He directs cold phrases at him, like a narcissistic scientist proud of his genius despite everything, even though, unlike in the novel, he hadn't killed anything Victor knew, and that Victor did feel a minimum of empathy for the monster. Everything about Victor and his surroundings is much more dehumanized, including him.

Instead, the Monster receives a certain lesson at his birth: the acceptance of the blind old man, even after learning his story; the affection and empathy of Elizabeth; the acceptance and final apology—something beautiful to see for those who have the injustice of the novel etched in their memory. His life is still awful, traumatic, but he receives much more appreciation than in the novel, and his purity is even more evident.

Speaking of Elizabeth, she's no longer that sickly, cheerful character who loves Victor almost out of obligation, but also with immense attachment. She's become a much freer thinker, much stronger, a protagonist, with a profound appreciation for all things life (something that was already present, but her interaction with the monster adds much more meaning to that quality of hers). And with a significant ending, where she manages to see the purity of the "monster" as no one else was able to. She rejects Victor, rejects his pathetic attempt to beg for forgiveness while he was obviously drowning in his hatred and delusions of God.

I also noticed something that might bother many: sometimes the makeup, the reactions at certain moments. Like Victor's brother throwing the moral lesson in his face quite directly before dying, how everyone moved aside when he was carrying Elizabeth. How he reached, Victor on the ship and no one seemed to have died on that occasion, the crew waiting outside for her to finish her story and then giving her space to leave without asking questions. But it didn't really bother me; I see it more as a play than a film, and in many scenes I get the feeling that was precisely the intention. To eliminate a certain semblance of realism, of logical reactions, to obtain instead a scene linked solely to art and not to coherence. Furthermore, the detail of Frankenstein's immortality and super strength initially seemed incoherent to me, but the way they lighten the burden of immortality later becomes something with great significance. Since the "monster" wasn't always alone, he received affection, but the burden was no longer just loneliness, but also eternity. The option of burning at the stake to ashes no longer exists; eternity is part of the condemnation that continues to make his life a hell, lacking the raw and pervasive loneliness of his namesake.

In conclusion, I'm pleasantly surprised by this true reinterpretation of a story I've always loved, but which has always caused me a lot of suffering. If I had to say something negative, it's that I might have liked to see a lot more expressiveness from the "monster" in some scenes, but since it's a face made up of different parts, and generally doesn't know how to physically react to feelings, I can accept it as it is.

Pokémon: Legends ZA (A quick surface review) Okay, so I’ll start with a few positives:

- I love the continuation of the story. I personally never got to play X and(/or) Y, but I like that the story continues 5 years in the future. It’s good to see where these stories have gone from many years ago!
- I like that you get to basically keep the integrity of the Legends series as main line games, but this feels like something fun.
- Real Time battles are super challenging, but are very exciting to play. The battling system is super fun.

In the middle reviews:
- Although exploring a city as big as Lumios is amazing (that includes climbing on the roofs and going into the catacombs), it feels a little monotoned. I would’ve loved to step out in at least 2 outer cities or forest areas to find more Pokémon, or get a different view than gray and brow buildings.
- I’m happy they brought back Mega Evolutions and Alpha Pokémon… what I *wish* they would’ve brought back were regional variants. Yes, we get an Alolan Raichu (it’s great), but I would’ve love some new Lumios regional Pokémon. I would’ve enjoyed a new Eeveelution as well. (That’s me being knit picky, I apologize).

In the low/bad reviews:
- I low-key wish Professor Sycamore was back instead of Mable. Yes, Mable is fun and looks as though she could be voiced by Grey Delisle, but I personally like Sycamore a bit more, not because he’s a man, but to continue the story of where he is…
- (SPOILER) I didn’t care for how they made the final boss be the tower. Like, yes, it’s different and it’s neat to see, but it’s also very… idk… Trope-ish? They put a lot of focus on the tower. I get it - it’s the main focal point. Yet, I - personally - wanted something different… (again that’s just me).

Overall review:
- It’s nice. I am having fun with the game and that’s all that matters. I’m ready to find my Shiny Eevee and more secrets!
